newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Air files lawsuit against ValuJet.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Air files lawsuit against ValuJet.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines Inc said on Friday it sued ValuJet Inc, alleging the discount carrier did not pay Kiwi for charter services provided in December.
Privately-held Kiwi, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September, said in the lawsuit that it never received $106,810 for services and contract fees for the charter flights.
ValuJet could not be immediately reached for comment.
In December, ValuJet contracted with Kiwi and other small carriers to provide charter services for flights on which it had sold tickets but did not have regulatory approval to operate.
The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration in December rejected ValuJet's plan to resume service between Atlanta and Dallas/Fort Worth, West Palm Beach or Fort Myers, Fla.
Kiwi said it provided charter services for ValuJet between Dec 19-21 for passengers who would have been stranded by the FAA ruling.
ValuJet was restricted to a limited service schedule after being grounded in late September in the wake of its May 11 crash in the Florida Everglades that killed all 110 people on board.
ValuJet spokesman Gregg Kenyon later said the company had not seen a copy of the lawsuit and has a policy of not commenting on pending litigation.
But Kenyon said Kiwi had "failed to operate reliably." He declined further comment.

In the lawsuit, which was filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J., Kiwi alleges that ValuJet's breach of contract caused Kiwi to sustain "substantial" damages in its relationships with its creditors, lender, vendors and customers.
Kiwi alleges that Valujet failed to pay for the charter services, the contract fee and the fees due for a cancelled agreement covering an additional 120 charter flights.
Kiwi alleges ValuJet owes about $260,000, including $91,810 for actual services provided, $15,000 in contract fees and $152,922 for cancelled flights.
Kiwi returned to regular commercial service on January 20.
ValuJet currently operates 112 daily departures to 19 cities. It plans to resume flight operations to Boston on February 20.
